03 / CONTAINERIZED INFRASTRUCTURE

Inception

A containerized service environment exploring service isolation, networking, persistent storage, and dependable configuration.

CONTAINERS / NETWORK / VOLUMES

CASE STUDY

  • Docker
  • Docker Compose
  • NGINX
  • Linux
  • Networking

Context

Inception is a systems project centred on building a small service environment from clearly separated containers.

Problem

Infrastructure is easy to make “work once”; the real challenge is making it understandable, isolated, and repeatable.

Solution

Services are defined around explicit responsibilities, connected through Docker networking, and supported by persistent storage where required.

My contribution

Worked through the practical relationship between service containers, reverse proxying, data persistence, and Linux-based operations.

Architecture

Docker Compose orchestrates the local environment, with NGINX serving as the front-facing routing layer.

Challenges

Working through network boundaries, volume behaviour, configuration dependencies, and startup order.

Lessons learned

The shape of the infrastructure affects how confidently a team can operate and evolve a system.
